title: EvenUp Raises $150M Series E at $2B+ Valuation to Redefine Personal Injury Law and Level the Playing Field for Injury Victims
author: EvenUp

kp.k: Investment expands in specialized personal injury AI
kp.d: EvenUp's October 7, 2025 company-issued announcement reports a $150 million Series E led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation including REV, RELX's venture capital arm. Total capital raised reached $385 million and valuation exceeded $2 billion, more than doubling in less than a year. The company interprets four investor-preempted financing rounds in two years as evidence of momentum and investor conviction.
qs: The funding brings EvenUp's total capital raised to $385 million and its valuation to over $2 billion—more than doubling in less than a year.
It also marks EvenUp's fourth financing round in just 2 years, each of them preempted by investors, underscoring both the company's momentum and the market's conviction in its mission.

kp.k: AI extends across the personal injury case lifecycle
kp.d: EvenUp describes its proprietary Piai model as trained on hundreds of thousands of injury cases and millions of medical records. It claims the platform proactively drafts, reviews and supports strategy throughout cases, automating documents and supplying insights while freeing attorneys to focus on client outcomes. These are the vendor's descriptions of capabilities and benefits.
qs: EvenUp's Claims Intelligence Platform™, powered by its proprietary Piai™ model, is trained on hundreds of thousands of injury cases and millions of medical records.
Unlike traditional tools, EvenUp's AI acts proactively, drafting, reviewing, and strategizing at superhuman scale across the entire case lifecycle.
Its Claims Intelligence Platform™ streamlines workflows, automates documents, and provides actionable insights across the entire case lifecycle.

kp.k: CEO claims revenue growth without additional staffing
kp.d: CEO Rami Karabibar reports that platform case volume nearly doubled in the preceding six months to 10,000 cases per week. He asserts that firms are increasing revenue without adding staff and that victims obtain better outcomes faster, framing AI as core practice infrastructure rather than an ancillary tool.
qs: In the last six months alone, case volume on our platform nearly doubled to 10,000 cases per week.
Firms are growing revenue without adding staff, while victims secure better results faster.

kp.k: Vendor reports substantial adoption and aggregate case outcomes
kp.d: EvenUp reports helping resolve more than 200,000 cases and securing over $10 billion in damages, with adoption by over 2,000 firms, including 20% of the Top 100 U.S. personal injury firms. It also reports ARR doubling year-over-year and aggregate case acceleration equivalent to many thousands of years of earlier resolutions. These figures are presented as company-reported impact and growth, not independent study findings.
qs: To date, EvenUp has helped resolve more than 200,000 cases, securing over $10 billion in damages for injury victims.
Today, over 2,000 firms—including 20% of the Top 100 U.S. personal injury firms—depend on EvenUp's platform.
With ARR doubling year-over-year, EvenUp is establishing itself as the AI platform of choice for modern PI law.

The result: the platform has already helped secure billions of dollars in settlements, accelerated case timelines by the equivalent of many thousands of years of earlier resolutions, and freed attorneys to focus on achieving the best outcomes for their clients.

kp.k: New products drive sales and replicate document workflows
kp.d: EvenUp reports that AI products launched earlier in 2025 account for nearly 90% of new sales and attributes growth to rapid product development. Its newly announced Mirror Mode allows firms to upload a successful draft and generate tailored versions preserving its language, style and structure, positioning prior firm work as a reusable basis for document production.
qs: EvenUp's newest AI products, launched earlier this year, are fueling rapid adoption and now account for nearly 90% of new sales—clear proof that product velocity is driving the company's growth.

By uploading a winning draft, firms can instantly generate tailored versions that mirror its language, style, and structure—delivering personalization at scale and ensuring every case begins from its strongest foundation.

kp.k: Customer attributes settlement improvement to real-time AI assistance
kp.d: In a testimonial carried by EvenUp, Kyle Wright of Wisehart Wright describes using Case Companion during mediation to challenge defense arguments, moving from an initial $50,000 offer to a $1.75 million settlement. This is a customer's account of a particular case, rather than a general measured effect. A second customer, John K. Zaid, describes platform integration from intake through resolution.
qs: "We went from an initial $50,000 offer to a $1.75 million settlement in mediation by using EvenUp's Case Companion to dismantle the defense's arguments in real time," said Kyle Wright, Managing Attorney at Wisehart Wright, Ohio.
EvenUp has become the backbone of our practice, driving us to operate at a higher level from intake to resolution.

kp.k: Investor predicts AI will become essential practice infrastructure
kp.d: Bessemer partner Sameer Dholakia describes EvenUp's vision as giving every personal injury attorney an AI partner drawing on accumulated case experience. Using word processors as an analogy, he predicts AI will become a basic requirement for practice and EvenUp a standard provider. This is an investor's prospective assessment, distinct from the announcement's reported adoption figures.
qs: "EvenUp's vision is to give every personal injury attorney a trusted AI partner, bringing the collective wisdom of hundreds of thousands of cases to every decision," said Sameer Dholakia, partner at Bessemer Venture Partners.
Just as word processors became essential, AI will soon be table stakes, and EvenUp will be the gold standard lawyers rely on.

kp.k: Justice-gap reduction is framed as a company mission
kp.d: EvenUp presents better representation and fairer outcomes for injury victims, delivered through technology supporting personal injury firms, as its access-to-justice mission. The statement expresses an intended contribution to closing the justice gap rather than reporting a measured reduction in unmet legal need.
qs: EvenUp is on a mission to close the justice gap with AI-powered technology that empowers personal injury firms to deliver higher standards of representation and fairer outcomes for millions of injury victims.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: EvenUp claims its AI supports work across the personal injury case lifecycle, accelerating resolutions and enabling firms to increase revenue without additional staff.
pts.d: In this company-issued release, EvenUp describes its Claims Intelligence Platform as proactively drafting, reviewing and strategizing, rather than simply responding as a traditional tool. It claims the platform frees attorneys to concentrate on client outcomes. CEO and co-founder Rami Karabibar specifically asserts that firms are growing revenue without adding staff and that victims obtain better results faster. This is a claim of increased capacity and lawyer augmentation, not an explicit prediction of layoffs or autonomous replacement of attorneys.

pts.k: EvenUp claims its newer products extend document generation and case insights across workflows, while Mirror Mode replicates a firm's preferred drafting patterns at scale.
pts.d: The company says its newer AI products can generate documents and surface insights that help cases settle faster with better outcomes. Mirror Mode, announced in the release, is claimed to generate tailored documents from an uploaded successful draft, preserving its language, style and structure. The company also attributes rapid adoption and growth to the pace of product development.

pts.k: Company and investor speakers frame AI as emerging core infrastructure for personal injury practice and predict that it will become a professional necessity.
pts.d: Karabibar says legal AI is becoming the backbone of personal injury law. Bessemer Venture Partners partner Sameer Dholakia predicts that AI will soon be as essential as word processors and that EvenUp will become the standard lawyers rely on. Dholakia describes the company's vision as giving every personal injury attorney an AI partner informed by accumulated case experience. Lightspeed partner Sebastian Duesterhoeft attributes EvenUp's prospective staying power to proprietary data, domain expertise and results. These are attributed strategic claims and predictions, rather than reported benchmark findings.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The release offers company-reported case outcomes, platform usage, adoption and commercial growth as evidence of impact and market uptake.
pts.d: EvenUp reports helping resolve more than 200,000 cases and securing over $10 billion in damages, with use by over 2,000 firms, including 20% of the Top 100 U.S. personal injury firms. Karabibar reports nearly doubled case volume over six months, reaching 10,000 cases weekly. The release also cites year-over-year ARR doubling and nearly 90% of new sales coming from products launched earlier in 2025. It describes training on hundreds of thousands of injury cases and millions of medical records. These are company-reported aggregate outcomes, usage and commercial indicators; the release supplies no comparative study, benchmark, calculation method for time savings, or quantified staffing and revenue analysis establishing the claimed productivity effects.

pts.k: Named customer testimonials supply a settlement example and accounts of practice-wide workflow improvements.
pts.d: Kyle Wright, managing attorney at Wisehart Wright in Ohio, attributes movement from a $50,000 initial offer to a $1.75 million mediated settlement to using Case Companion to challenge defense arguments in real time. He also reports meaningful monthly workflow improvements from new releases. John K. Zaid, managing partner and founder of John K. Zaid & Associates in Texas, describes higher-level operations from intake through resolution. These are customer accounts presented in the company release; no controlled comparison or further case documentation is provided.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: Operational benefits are presented as already occurring by October 7, 2025; AI's universal necessity is an undated near-term prediction.
pts.d: The release dates cumulative case outcomes and firm adoption to publication on October 7, 2025. Case-volume growth covers the preceding six months, while ARR growth is year-over-year. The newer products launched earlier in 2025, and Mirror Mode was unveiled on the publication date. Mirror Mode's described customization requires uploading a winning draft. Dholakia's prediction uses 'soon' without a deadline. Claims about better outcomes and revenue growth are framed around firms using the platform; the release does not specify verification requirements, accuracy thresholds or circumstances in which those benefits would not hold.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The claimed beneficiaries are personal injury firms and attorneys through greater capacity, and injury victims through faster, fairer and higher-quality representation and outcomes.
pts.d: The source concerns personal injury practice, with adoption evidence specifically referencing U.S. firms. EvenUp is positioned as a technology provider to firms, not as an alternative legal service provider delivering representation itself. Attorneys are said to gain drafting and strategic assistance, while firms can expand revenue without staff additions. Injury victims are said to receive better results sooner. The company separately states a mission to close the justice gap for millions of victims; it does not report a measure of previously unmet legal need being served or demonstrate expanded access for people unable to obtain counsel.
